longest_story.title: Endings!
longest_story.first_line: For the Hobgoblin, it began with the discovery of the journals of the late Norman Osborn, the original Green Goblin.
longest_story.characters: Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (antagonist); J. Jonah Jameson; Harry Osborn; Robbie Robertson; Spider-Man [Peter Parker]
longest_story.synopsis: Hobgoblin has blown up Green Goblin's lair and escaped in his battle van. Spider-Man makes his way into the van. It crashes into the river and explodes as Spider-Man escapes. Spider-Man tries to save Hobgoblin but is only able to find his mask. Spider-Man arrives at the Bugle and discovers that J. Jonah Jameson has already printed his crime (the creation of the Scorpion). Jonah has turned the reins over to Robbie and will solely function as the Bugle's publisher. Spider-Man swings into Central Park to find a giant alien complex that he feels compelled to enter. He is off to the Secret Wars.
longest_story.notes: Cont. in Marvel Super-Heroes Secret Wars (Marvel, 1984 Series) #1

longest_story.title: Homecoming
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Venom symbiote (introduction, as the black costume); Curt Connors [Lizard]; Billy Connors; Martha Connors; Black Cat [Felicia Hardy]; J. Jonah Jameson; Robbie Robertson; Aunt May Parker; Nathan Lubensky; The Avengers [Captain America [Steve Rogers]; Thor; Iron Man [James Rhodes]; Hawkeye; Wasp; Captain Marvel [Monica Rambeau]]; She-Hulk (cameo, in photo); Mr. Fantastic (cameo, in photo); Human Torch [Johnny Storm] (cameo, in photo); The Thing (cameo, in photo); Invisible Girl (cameo, in photo); Cyclops (cameo, in photo); Colossus (cameo, in photo); Wolverine (cameo, in photo); Storm (cameo, in photo); Nightcrawler (cameo, in photo); Mockingbird (cameo, in photo); Scarlet Witch (cameo, in photo); Weezie; Justin
longest_story.synopsis: Spider-Man returns from Secret Wars and tries to get used to his new black and white symbiotic costume, which will later become Venom.
longest_story.notes: Continued from Marvel Super-Heroes Secret Wars (Marvel, 1984 series) #12. 1st in black costume which later becomes Venom. Predates Secret Wars #8 by 7 months. Next chronological Spidey in black duds in Marvel Team-Up #141.

longest_story.title: By Myself Betrayed!
longest_story.first_line: Time is running out for the Mammoths, Bill!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Aunt May Parker; Wendy Thorton (first appearance); Robbie Robertson; Betty Leeds; Nathan Lubensky; Rose (first appearance, villain); Black Cat (cameo, flashback); Uncle Ben Parker (cameo, flashback); Ray Nesters; Tony Nesters; Bob Clayton; Johnston; Varley
longest_story.synopsis: While on the sports beat with Wendy, Peter gets involved in a scandal with a pro football quarterback who is throwing games for a new mob boss, the Rose. Peter tells Aunt May that he has dropped out of school and she flips out. Peter also discovers that Robbie is taking his new editor-in-chief position at the Bugle very seriously. Spider-Man meets and battles the Rose for the first time.

longest_story.title: With Great Power...
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Aunt May Parker; Nathan Lubensky; Betty Leeds; Wendy Thorton; Robbie Robertson; Jack O' Lantern [Jason Macendale Jr.] (villain); Roderick Kingsley [Hobgoblin] (cameo); Black Cat [Felicia Hardy] (cameo flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: Spider-Man watches as the authorities pull Hobgoblin's wrecked battle van from the Hudson River. When the van is stolen in broad daylight, Spider-Man tracks it down and finds it has been taken by Jack O' Lantern. Spider-Man battles Jack but this causes him to miss a dinner set up by Nathan where he was supposed to be making nice with Aunt May who is still furious over Peter dropping out of school.

longest_story.title: Even a Ghost Can Fear the Night!
longest_story.first_line: Silent as a living shadow, he glides through the night.
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Red Ghost (villain); Super Apes (villain); Black Fox (villain); Aunt May Parker (cameo); Nathan Lubensky (cameo); Roderick Kingsley [Hobgoblin] (cameo); Jack O' Lantern [Jason Macendale Jr.] (cameo flashback); Iron Man [James Rhodes] (cameo flashback); Mr. Fantastic (cameo flashback); Invisible Girl (cameo flashback); Human Torch [Johnny Storm] (cameo flashback); The Thing (cameo flashback); Black Cat [Felicia Hardy] (cameo flashback); Mamie Muggins
longest_story.synopsis: The Black Fox is on his final burglary, the one that will allow him to retire, but unfortunately, he has chosen the residence of the Red Ghost and his Super Apes. The Red Ghost compels the Fox to work with his Apes in carrying out the robbery of a jewelry store to fund his latest invention, the Cosmicizer. Spider-Man intervenes, follows the Apes home and blows up the Ghost's pet project. All but forgotten, the Black Fox merrily makes off with the jewels.

longest_story.title: Introducing... Puma!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Black Cat [Felicia Hardy]; Jenna Taylor; Robbie Robertson; Betty Leeds; Mary Jane Watson; The Rose (villain); Puma [Thomas Fireheart] (villain, introduction); Aunt May Parker (cameo flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: Spider-Man takes down another one of the Rose's operations and the mob boss calls in wealthy businessman and super powered assassin Thomas Fireheart a.k.a. The Puma to kill the web slinger. Exhausted, Peter crawls into bed for a good night's sleep but his alien costume seems to have other ideas. Robbie commends Peter on his nice photos (they were taken by the Black Cat) but Peter is so tired that he barely notices. Spider-Man is ambushed by the Puma and pulls his left arm out of its socket. With Spider-Man down and writhing in pain, the Puma prepares to pounce.

longest_story.title: Beware the Claws of Puma!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Black Cat [Felicia Hardy]; Jenna Taylor; Mary Jane Watson; The Rose (villain); Puma [Thomas Fireheart] (villain); Kingpin (villain); Arranger (villain); Hobgoblin [Ned Leeds] (cameo)
longest_story.synopsis: Puma is about to eviscerate Spider-Man but the Black Cat swings in to the rescue. Spidey and the Cat make it back to his apartment. The Black Cat takes off but Mary Jane shows up to hang out. As the Puma strikes Peter pushes Mary Jane out the door. Spidey and Puma fight but the assassin breaks off the attack when he witnesses Spider-Man save civilians. The Kingpin discovers that the Rose has put out an unauthorized contract on Spidey's life. Fireheart returns home. Hobgoblin contacts Rose. Peter finds Mary Jane still at his apartment where she tells him that she already knows he is Spider-Man.

longest_story.title: The Sinister Secret of Spider-Man's New Costume!
longest_story.first_line: All in all, it's been a rotten week for Peter Parker.
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Black Cat [Felicia Hardy]; Mary Jane Watson; Thomas Fireheart [Puma]; Jenna Taylor; Fantastic Four [Mister Fantastic; Human Torch [Johnny Storm]]; H.U.B.E.R.T.; Hobgoblin [Ned Leeds] (villain); Rose (villain); Aunt May Parker (cameo flashback); Robbie Robertson (cameo flashback); Jack O' Lantern [Jason Macendale Jr.] (cameo flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: Peter is floored by Mary Jane’s revelation that she knows he is Spider-Man. The Black Cat shows up at his pad and Mary Jane takes off. Peter decides to have Mr. Fantastic check it out the black costume. Reed Richards discovers that Spider-Man's black costume is an alien that is trying to bond with him symbiotically. He uses a sonic blaster to separate Spider-Man from his costume. Spider-Man swings home in an old Fantastic Four uniform with a paper bag for a mask. Mary Jane drops by to talk. Hobgoblin has a little proposition for the Rose.
longest_story.keywords: Baxter Building; black costume; paper bag

longest_story.title: All My Pasts Remembered!
longest_story.first_line: I'm real glad we finally got this chance to talk, Peter.
longest_story.characters: Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (villain); Harry Osborn (flashback) (cameo); Liz Osborn (flashback) (cameo); Aunt May Parker (flashback) (cameo); The Rose [Richard Fisk] (villain); Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Anna Watson (flashback) (cameo); Gayle Watson (flashback); Madeline Watson (flashback); Mary Jane Watson (origin); Philip Watson (flashback); Frank Brown (flashback); Timothy Byrnes (flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: As Peter struggles with the fact that Mary Jane knows he is Spider-Man, she opens up for the first time and tells him her family's history full of heartbreak, abuse and abandonment. Mr. Fantastic tries to communicate telepathically with Spider-Man's alien costume but has no success. Hobgoblin demands a cut of crime operations all over the city to sweeten his new business deal with the Rose. He then sets his sights on Harry Osborn. Learning that the Hobgoblin is still alive, Peter dons his classic red and blue costume as Spider-Man and prepares to face his old foe.

longest_story.title: The Challenge of Hobgoblin!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Aunt May Parker; Arthur Chekov; Harry Osborn; Liz Osborn; Mary Jane Watson; Franklin Richards; Invisible Girl; Betty Leeds; Ann MacIntosh; J. Jonah Jameson; Robbie Robertson; Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (villain); Rose (villain); Black Cat (cameo flashback); Green Goblin [Norman Osborn] (cameo flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: Spidey cuts through the New York underworld looking for Hobgoblin. Spidey's black alien costume tries to get young Franklin Richards to free it from containment but fails. Hobgoblin attacks Harry looking for more of his dad's Goblin journals but Spidey intervenes. They take their fight to the women's bathroom where Hobby has to extinguish a pumpkin bomb webbed to his hand in the toilet. Hobgoblin tries to get away but Spidey snags his goblin glider. Hobby retaliates by slamming Spidey into the side of a train. Liz and Mary Jane are captured by the Rose's men and Harry is powerless to stop it.

longest_story.title: The Sins of My Father!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Harry Osborn; Liz Osborn; Mary Jane Watson; Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (villain); Rose (villain); Green Goblin [Norman Osborn] (cameo flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: The Rose and Hobgoblin have captured Liz and Mary Jane and Harry has to trade their lives for his dad's old Goblin journals. Hobby is mad at only getting one journal as he knocks Harry out and takes him back to the Rose's headquarters. Harry attacks the villain using his own weapons. A fire breaks out in the warehouse trapping Mary Jane and Liz; the latter goes into labor. Spidey takes over Harry's battle with the Hobgoblin. Hobgoblin gets away as Spider-Man gets his pals out of the building. Liz and Harry head for the hospital. Spidey's black alien costume escapes from the Baxter Building.

longest_story.title: Trade Secret
longest_story.inks: Bob Layton (credited as Layton); Carlos Garzón (credited as Garzon)
longest_story.characters: Uncle Ben Parker (flashback); Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Ben Urich; D.J. Jones; Roberto DeNatale
longest_story.synopsis: A sleazy photographer snaps a picture of Peter changing out of his Spider-Man costume and Spider-Man has to stop him before he can peddle his secret identity to the criminal underworld.
longest_story.notes: In case you didn't notice, the mob boss in this story has the same name as the comic's assistant editor.

longest_story.title: The Spectacular Spider-Kid!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Spider-Kid [Ollie Osnick]; Black Cat [Felicia Hardy]; Harry Osborn; Liz Osborn; Normie Osborn (introduction); Mary Jane Watson; Blazing Skull Gang (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: A chubby, outcast kid who used to idolize Doc Ock now dons a Spider-Man costume and his octopus arms to make a bid to become Spider-Man’s sidekick. Things don't work out for the partnership but Spider-Man is able to help him out a bit in his personal life. Much to the relief of her husband and her friends, Liz delivers a healthy baby boy.

longest_story.title: Red 9 and Red Tape!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Philmont Magee; Doctor Rattamun; Mr. Blodgett; Cheryl Swanson; Wendall; Mindy; Judge Benjamin Handley; Red 9 (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: Spider-Man has his hands full with a hopped up Texas teenager in a souped up super suit who’s itching to prove himself by taking our hero down. At the same time, he also cuts through a mile of red tape to bring an old man back to life (on paper at least).

longest_story.title: After the Fox!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Silver Sable (introduction); Wild Pack (introduction); Morty Sable (introduction); Black Fox; Aunt May Parker; Nathan Lubensky; Harry Osborn; Liz Osborn; Normie Osborn; Mary Jane Watson; Black Cat [Felicia Hardy] (cameo flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: The Black Fox is still trying to complete the final score that will allow him to retire but finds himself being chased by Silver Sable and her Wild Pack. Falling for Fox's sob story about missing his family, Spider-Man helps him escape but returns the jewels he stole to Silver Sable. Peter begins to reconnect with Aunt May who has shunned him after he told her he dropped out of grad school.

longest_story.title: Jump for My Love or Spring Is in the Air
longest_story.colors: Glynis Oliver (credited as Oliver); Nel Yomtov (credited as Yomtov)
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Black Cat [Felicia Hardy]; Toad; Frog-Man; Spider-Kid
longest_story.synopsis: Spider-Man saves Toad from committing suicide, and Toad decides to try to become his sidekick. Spider-Man blows him off until the next day, and Toad recruits a gang of thugs to attack Spider-Man so he can show his worth to the web slinger. Frog-Man gets wise to the plot and shows up to help out. So does Spider-Kid. Finding a point of commonality amongst themselves, Toad, Frog-Man and Spider-Kid decide to become a new super team: the Misfits. Shaking his head in disbelief, Spider-Man is all too happy to simply walk away from the ludicrous situation.

longest_story.title: The Commuter Cometh!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Human Torch [Johnny Storm]; The Commuter (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: Spider-Man commutes all the way out to the suburbs by train, bus, taxi and garbage truck to catch a middle-aged thief.

longest_story.title: This Gold Is Mine!
longest_story.inks: Joe Rubinstein (credited as Josef Rubinstein) (finished art)
longest_story.first_line: Whu... what's going on?  Why won't you let me pass?
longest_story.characters: Charles Anderson (also in flashback); Arranger [Oswald Silkworth] (villain); Beyonder (cameo flashback); Betty Brant-Leeds; Firelord [Pyreus Kril] (cameo); J. Jonah Jameson; Kingpin [Wilson Fisk] (villain, flashback); Ned Leeds; Robbie Robertson; Spider-Man [Peter Parker] (also in flashback); Sgt. Conrad S. Hauser [Duke]; Joe; Judy
longest_story.synopsis: The Beyonder has turned a downtown building and all of its contents into solid gold and the government scrambles to keep this fact a secret in order to keep the world from plunging into an economic crisis. The building is being carved up and the gold dropped into a deep sea chasm to take it out of play. Spider-Man helps Agent Anderson foil a plot by the Kingpin to steal a load of the gold for himself. Peter, however, has taken a solid gold notebook he found in the trash home with him and tries to figure out what to do with it.
longest_story.notes: Secret Wars II Crossover; Cont from Web of Spider-Man (Marvel, 1985 series) #6; Story takes place between Secret Wars (Marvel, 1985 series) #2 and 3; One of the soldiers directing the cleanup of the golden building is simply referred to as "Sergeant" in the story but is pretty clearly intended to be Duke of the G.I. Joe team.

longest_story.title: Burn, Spider, Burn!
longest_story.characters: Aunt May Parker; the Beyonder (flashback); Firelord; Nathan Lubensky; Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Victor; Martha; Sophie; Nathan

longest_story.title: The Hero and the Holocaust!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Firelord; J. Jonah Jameson; Robbie Robertson; Betty Leeds; Kathryn Cushing; The Avengers [Captain America [Steve Rogers]; Black Knight [Dane Whitman]; Hercules; Wasp; Starfox]; Agent Raymond Sikorski
longest_story.synopsis: Spider-Man has a rematch with Firelord and tries to beat the former Herald of Galactus before the cosmic powered being kills him. The Avengers show up to lend a hand but arrive too late to effect the battle.
longest_story.keywords: Grand Central Station; National Security Council

longest_story.title: Whatever Happened to Crusher Hogan?
longest_story.inks: Joe Rubinstein (credited as Josef Rubinstein) (finished art)
longest_story.first_line: I'll never forget the first time I laid eyes on the kid.
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Crusher Hogan; Bobby Chance; Aunt May Parker; Nathan Lubensky; Mary Jane Watson; Lance Bannon; Ned Leeds; Betty Leeds; Manslaughter Marsdale (villain); Madame Fang (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: Crusher Hogan is working maintenance at a boxing facility and spinning tall tales of how he helped create Spider-Man when he discovers a plot by one of the owners to take down a fighter. Peter gets a call from May who asks him to keep an eye on Nathan who may be in trouble. Spider-Man gets involved in the problems Crusher Hogan and Bobby Chance are having with Manslaughter. Felling the villain, Spider-Man tells a white lie that confirms his "close" relationship with Hogan, making him a hero. Peter tells Aunt May he lost track of Nathan and finds he was beaten badly and is now in the hospital.

longest_story.title: Make Way for Slyde!
longest_story.characters: Thomas Fireheart (cameo); Nathan Lubensky; Aunt May; Uncle Ben Parker (flashback) (cameo); Slyde [Jalome Beacher] (origin) (villain) (introduction); Spider-Man [Peter Parker] (featured); Jenna Taylor (cameo); Joseph Threetrees (introduction); Blake Tower; Rockwall (villain); Kisani Tribe (introduction)
longest_story.synopsis: Spider-Man takes on a slippery new villain who ends up looking like a good guy when he turns his old boss over to D.A. Tower. Thomas Fireheart prepares to face the Beyonder.

longest_story.title: To Challenge the Beyonder!
longest_story.inks: Joe Rubinstein (credited as Josef Rubinstein) (finished art)
longest_story.first_line: Somewhere on a small Indian reservation located forty-three miles...
longest_story.characters: Absorbing Man [Crusher Creel] (cameo flashback); Lance Bannon; Beyonder (also in flashback); Betty Brant-Leeds; Bulldozer [Henry Camp] (cameo flashback); Captain America [Steve Rogers] (cameo flashback); Arthur Chekov; Kathryn Cushing; Hulk [Bruce Banner] (cameo flashback); Kang [Nathaniel Richards] (Other Earth - Earth-6311) (cameo flashback); Ned Leeds; Nathan Lubensky; Mamie Muggins; Aunt May Parker; Puma [Thomas Fireheart] (also in flashback); Spider-Man [Peter Parker] (also in flashback); Jenna Taylor; Flash Thompson; Thor [Thor Odinson] (cameo flashback); Ben Urich; Mary Jane Watson; Wolverine [Logan] (cameo flashback); Phil; Clifton; Arnold; Victor; Harriet; Barry Foxe; Lynn; Mr. Chumley
longest_story.synopsis: Puma arrives in New York to fulfill his destiny: to kill the Beyonder. He contacts former foe Spider-Man for help and the pair investigate a new cult that seems to have been started by the Beyonder. Spider-Man is disgusted when the cosmic entity is nowhere to be found and leaves Puma to his own devices. Puma meets the Beyonder who blinks him instantly to Japan. Puma flies back to New York City and tries to convince Spider-Man that the Beyonder has to be stopped immediately.
longest_story.notes: Continued from Secret Wars II (Marvel, 1985 series) #7. Continued in Spectacular Spider-Man (Marvel, 1976 series) #111.

longest_story.title: Lo, There Shall Come a Champion!
longest_story.pencils: Ron Frenz (credited) (layouts); Tom Morgan (credited) (finished pencils); James Fry (credited) (finished pencils); Jack Fury (art assist)
longest_story.inks: Joe Rubinstein (credited) (finishes); John Romita (credited); Russ Steffens (credited) (background inks)
longest_story.first_line: Prologue: somewhere in the desert southwest of Hartsdale, New Mexico...
longest_story.characters: Arranger [Oswald Silkworth] (villain); Beyonder; Doctor Strange [Stephen Strange] (cameo flashback); Eternity (cameo flashback); Thomas Fireheart; Green Goblin [Norman Osborn] (villain, Zarathos illusion); Kingpin [Wilson Fisk] (villain); Nathan Lubensky; Mephisto (villain); Molecule Man [Owen Reece] (cameo flashback); Aunt May Parker; Mary Parker (villain, Zarathos illusion); Richard Parker (villain, Zarathos illusion); Uncle Ben Parker (villain, Zarathos illusion); Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Captain George Stacy (villain, Zarathos illusion); Gwen Stacy (villain, Zarathos illusion); The Watcher [Uatu] (cameo flashback); Anna Watson; Mary Jane Watson; Zarathos (villain); Marty
longest_story.synopsis: The Beyonder makes a deal with the devil: he agrees not to destroy the cosmos if a hero can sustain his life's purpose in the face of overwhelming adversity. He chooses Spidey and frees Zarathos to torment him. Spidey overhears plans for the murder of Kingpin. Resolved to rescue him, Spidey is hampered in his quest by dead friends and foes from the past who accuse him of being a failure. Spidey is beaten down and begins to give in to despair. The source of the illusions, Zarathos, confronts Spider-Man and tries to convince him to let Kingpin be killed. Spidey finds the strength to fight back.
longest_story.notes: Continued from Secret Wars II (Marvel, 1985 series) #8; Continued in Secret Wars II (Marvel, 1985 series) #9.

longest_story.title: The Choice and The Challenge!
longest_story.inks: Joe Rubinstein (credited as Josef Rubinstein) (finished art); Steve Ditko
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Aunt May Parker; Uncle Ben Parker (flashback); Nathan Lubensky; Mary Jane Watson; Arthur Chekov; Flash Thompson; Sha Shan; Crusher Hogan (flashback); Liz Allan (flashback); Betty Leeds; Robbie Robertson; Ned Leeds; Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (villain); Rose (villain); Kingpin (villain); Arranger (villain); Green Goblin [Norman Osborn] (cameo flashback); Gwen Stacy (cameo flashback); Jean DeWolff (cameo flashback); Sin-Eater (cameo flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: The Hobgoblin prepares to bring down Spider-Man. Peter and Aunt May bring Nathan home from the hospital. Peter tells Mary Jane that he is through being Spider-Man and tells her his origin story. Flash smacks his girlfriend around and busts Ned Leeds in the chops when he confronts him about the affair Flash is having with his wife. Hobgoblin takes Sha Shan as a hostage. Mary Jane convinces Peter that he can't quit with the Hobgoblin on the loose so Spidey faces his old foe. Spidey is able to rescue Sha Shan but is brought down by Hobby's new chest plate with a deadly random pattern blaster.

longest_story.title: Unmasked!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Mary Jane Watson; Flash Thompson [also as Hobgoblin]; Sha Shan; Robbie Robertson; Betty Leeds; Lance Bannon; Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (villain); Rose (villain); Scourge (villain); Human Fly (death)
longest_story.synopsis: Hobgoblin and Spider-Man have it out and Spider-Man ends up unmasking his foe. He is shocked to discover that one of his deadliest foes is really one of his oldest pals, Flash Thompson (or is he?). Scourge kills the Human Fly.

longest_story.title: Cry of the Wendigo
longest_story.first_line: You are running, and it is cold, very cold.
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Askwith family [Mr. Askwith; Mrs. Askwith; Askwiths' daughter]; Wendigo spirit
longest_story.notes: This Wendigo is not the Marvel monster/villain but is instead a spirit entity.

longest_story.title: If This Be Justice
longest_story.script: Tom DeFalco (credited) (plot); Peter David (credited); Jo Duffy (credited)
longest_story.letters: Rick Parker (credited as Parker); Joe Rosen (credited as Rosen)
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Betty Leeds; Lance Bannon; Robbie Robertson; Ned Leeds; Kathryn Cushing; Flash Thompson; Scourge (villain); Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (villain); Rose (villain); Wraith [Brian DeWolff] (villain, death)
longest_story.synopsis: Scourge breaks into prison to kill Flash Thompson for being the Hobgoblin, but ends up killing the Wraith instead after Spider-Man interferes.

longest_story.title: Savage Is the Sable!
longest_story.characters: Silver Sable; Wild Pack; Morty Sable; J. Jonah Jameson; Robbie Robertson; Jasper Cornbluth; Mary Jane Watson; Joy Mercado; Jack O' Lantern [Jason Macendale Jr.] (villain); Spider-Man [Peter Parker] (cameo flashback); Machine Man (cameo flashback)
longest_story.synopsis: With Spidey MIA, Silver Sable takes on both killer robbers and Jack O' Lantern by herself.
longest_story.notes: Missing in Action cross-over; Continued from The Spectacular Spider-Man (Marvel, 1976 series) #117; Continued in Web of Spider-Man (Marvel, 1985 series) #18

longest_story.title: Introducing the Sinister Syndicate!
longest_story.colors: Paul Becton (credited as Paul J. Becton)
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Silver Sable; Sandman; Flash Thompson; Sha-Shan; Betty Brant Leeds; Ned Leeds; Sinister Syndicate [Beetle [Abner Jenkins]; Rhino; Hydro-Man; Boomerang; Speed Demon [James Saunders]] (villain); Kingpin (villain); Arranger (villain); Jason Macendale [Jack O' Lantern] (villain); Roderick Kingsley (villain); Daniel Kingsley (villain, in shadow)
longest_story.synopsis: In order to raise some money to help Flash mount his defense, Spider-Man is hired by Silver Sable to help her bring in Jack O' Lantern. Instead, they find themselves up against five of Spider-Man’s foes calling themselves the Sinister Syndicate. Ned leaves Betty. Macendale tries to peddle his services as Jack O' Lantern to the Kingpin and the Rose but is unsuccessful. Sandman is out for a suburban stroll when he notices the Sinister Syndicate drop a roller coaster on Spider-Man and Sable.

longest_story.title: When Warriors Clash--!
longest_story.characters: Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Silver Sable; Sandman; J. Jonah Jameson; Robbie Robertson; Flash Thompson; Hobgoblin [Ned Leeds] (villain); Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (villain); Jack O'Lantern [Jason Macendale Jr.] (villain); Rose (villain); Sinister Syndicate [Beetle [Abner Jenkins]; Rhino; Hydro-Man; Boomerang; Speed Demon [James Saunders]] (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: Sandman helps Spider-Man and Silver Sable fight off the Sinister Syndicate. Jack O' Lantern frees Flash Thompson from jail, thinking he is the Hobgoblin. The real Hobgoblin intervenes and a battle ensues.

longest_story.title: The Fury of X-Factor!
longest_story.first_line: 6:30 A.M.: arrested and imprisoned for the crimes of the Hobgoblin,
longest_story.characters: X-Factor [Angel [Warren Worthington III]; Beast [Hank McCoy]; Cyclops [Scott Summers]; Iceman [Bobby Drake]; Marvel Girl [Jean Grey]]; Sharon Banks; Betty Brant-Leeds; Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (picture); Cameron Hodge; J. Jonah Jameson; Alfredo Morelli (first appearance); Rhino [Aleksei Sytsevich] (cameo flashback); Robbie Robertson; Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Flash Thompson (picture); Mary Jane Watson; Captain Keating
longest_story.synopsis: In the wake of Flash Thompson's escape, everyone is looking for the man believed to be the Hobgoblin. Jameson hires X-Factor to bring in Spider-Man by telling them he is a mutant. Still reeling from his battle with Rhino, Spider-Man takes on X-Factor.

longest_story.title: With Foes Like These...
longest_story.characters: Absorbing Man [Crusher Creel] (villain); Lance Bannon; Kathryn Cushing; Dr. Doom [Victor Von Doom] (cameo); Hobgoblin [Roderick Kingsley] (villain); Kris Keating (The Foreigner in disguise); Daniel Kingsley (posing as his brother Roderick); Betty Leeds; Ned Leeds; Mongoose (cameo) (introduction, shadow only); Robbie Robertson; Spider-Man [Peter Parker] (featured); Flash Thompson; Titania [Mary MacPherran] (villain); Wasp [Janet Van Dyne]; Mary Jane Watson
longest_story.synopsis: Spider-Man is trolling around town trying to find Flash Thompson but ends up duking it out with Titania and Absorbing Man. Things end in a draw when Absorbing Man threatens to drop an airplane full of passengers and Spider-Man swings away in disgust.

longest_story.title: ...And Who Shall Stand Against Them...?

longest_story.inks: Brett Breeding; Joe Rubinstein (credited as Josef Rubinstein)

longest_story.synopsis: Spidey faces a drug den while searching for Daredevil. Matt shows up for lunch at Aunt May's and they have a shouting match that comes to blows. Hobgoblin catches a man bugging the Kingpin's building. Lance tells him that the Kingpin is coming back to town. Spidey begins to battle Kingpin only to discover that it's actually Daredevil. The two heroes duel until DD appears to save Spidey's life. DD assures Spidey that they will take the Kingpin down legally. Kingpin is secreted home safely. Kingpin meets the Hobgoblin who provides the true identity of the Rose, but Kingpin already knew.

longest_story.synopsis: The gang war seems to settle down as the Kingpin has returned to take over his operations. Hobgoblin and Jack O' Lantern clash. Kingpin confronts his son and rival mob boss, the Rose. Kingpin calls a meeting of all of his lieutenants and is preparing to have them gunned down when Spider-Man, Daredevil and the Falcon intervene. Spider-Man shouts it out with Kingpin but it is Daredevil who has the last word.

longest_story.title: The Hobgoblin Revealed!

longest_story.synopsis: Ned Leeds' body is returned to the United States, and his family and friends attend his funeral. Peter takes Betty home but finds she is becoming more and more unstable. The new Hobgoblin takes out the Rose's men. Kingpin gives Spider-Man the file proving Leeds was Hobgoblin. Hobgoblin comes after Spider-Man for the file, and it gets burned up in their battle. Flash Thompson is cleared of the charges that he was Hobgoblin. Peter decides to continue to fight crime as Spider-Man.
longest_story.notes:
Story continues from Spider-Man vs. Wolverine (Marvel, 1987 series) #1.

This issue reveals that that Hobgoblin was Ned Leeds, sort of. After four years of hints, clues and red herrings, somebody had to be under the yellow Goblin mask. Original Hobgoblin creator Roger Stern left the comic without telling anyone his ideas on the true identity of the villain. Tom DeFalco, who wrote many of the issues leading up to this revelation, had an alleged falling out with editor Jim Owsley and quit the book without providing the identity of who he intended to be Hobgoblin. According to Peter David, he was told to write this unmasking story, and Owsley intended for the secret identity of the Hobgoblin to be the Foreigner. This made no sense to David, and they tried to hash out who actually could be the villain; Ned Leeds became the only viable suspect (and was a fan-favorite for the role), but Owsley had already written the Spider-Man vs. Wolverine one-shot in which Leeds was killed. It was up to Peter David to paint Ned as the culprit posthumously.

Ten years later (1997), original Hobgoblin scribe Roger Stern returned to the character in the Hobgoblin Lives limited series. In this story, he does a little creative rewriting of history (retroactive continuity), and he reveals that Ned Leeds was simply a brainwashed dupe of the real Hobgoblin, narcissistic fashion designer Roderick Kingsley. Ironically, Kingsley is the only person according to the original stories who could not have been the Hobgoblin, as he was seen on two occasions to be working with the villain and talking to him without his mask. Stern introduced a secret twin brother, Daniel, in Hobgoblin Lives who impersonated Roderick at key moments and made the Kingsly-as-Hobgoblin theory at least mildly plausible.

This is Marvel's official version of the Hobgoblin controversy, and the convoluted appearance list issue by issue can be seen under the Hobgoblin character profile on Marvel's official site here: http://www.marvunapp.com/Appendix5/hobgoblinkingsley.htm. Peter David discusses the story for this issue and the Leeds/Hobgoblin decision here: http://www.peterdavid.net/archives/002234.html.
